transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-05 14:00 UTC / Duration 60m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Ravi (Quartz Foundry lead ML), Elena (Product PM), Samir (Infra), Jill (Finance)
Links shared: pilot-benchmarks.csv, cost-model-v2.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4, security-appendix.pdf

Summary: Quick sync on pilot economics. Diego ran two new runs overnight with prefix caching and micro-batching. Initial numbers show meaningful token savings from prefix/KV cache but some tail latency regression when batching more aggressively. Customer to share traffic trace and decide on next benchmark variants.

Topics: tokens/sec/$, KV/prefix caching, micro-batching vs continuous batching, sequence length distribution, quantization quality impact, Dedicated vs Hosted routing, SLOs/finance questions on cost predictability

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for making time today, we'll go 60 minutesish, want to cover the overnight runs diego did and then talk next steps on benchmarks and pricing.
[00:22] Diego: yeah i pushed three configs last night. baseline was hosted gpt-small-ish open model, no kv cache, 1-token batching window. run A was prefix cache enabled with 8k prefix retention, run B added micro-batching 32-token windows, run C was micro-batch + quantized fp16->4bit experiment.
[00:48] Ravi: quick question on nomenclature, when you say prefix cache is that the same as the kv cache we've been testing, the k-v cash, yeah that thing?
[01:05] Diego: yes, same. sometimes the auto transcription makes it k-v cash. it's the KV cache / prefix caching. saves tokens for repeated context across requests like chat threads.
[01:20] Elena: high level before numbers — what's our target tokens per dollar for production? Jill or finance do you have a target?
[01:33] Jill: from our back-of-envelope we need 1.5M tokens per $ to hit target margins for the pilot. Ideally 2M+ for expansion. but we can accept lower if latency is better.
[01:45] Diego: okay numbers. Baseline tokens/sec/$ roughly 1.2M tokens per dollar. With prefix cache (run A) we saw tokens/$ -> 1.6M, so ~33% improvement. micro-batching (run B) added throughput but only +12% tokens/$ to 1.8M, BUT p95 latency moved from ~220ms to ~340ms. quantized run (run C) pushed tokens/$ to ~2.1M but quality diffs need human eval, hallucination slightly higher in short sampling.
[02:20] Ravi: 340ms p95 is pretty high for interactive flows. Our target is p95 <= 250ms for customer-facing chat.
[02:31] Diego: understood. the micro-batching config trades off tail latency. The runtime uses continuous batching so micro-batching increases batching window slightly and that bumps tail. There's also kernel packing effects on certain sequence lengths.
[02:47] Maya: can we get the p95 w/ batching but with smaller windows? like 16-token micro-batches instead of 32?
[02:55] Diego: yeah that's the next variant — 16-token micro-batches look promising. early sims show p95 ~270ms and tokens/$ ~1.95M. so middle ground.
[03:12] Samir: network-wise, when you increase micro-batch window, does that affect CPU networking on the host? I'm worried about our VPC peering and MTU inconsistencies adding jitter to tail latency.
[03:26] Diego: it can. we saw occasional jitter on the host path when sequence lengths burst. In Dedicated runs we had slightly more stable p95 due to homogenous HW. Hosted had more variability across AZs.
[03:41] Ravi: what about fallback behaviors? e.g., route to a smaller model variant on overload or use cached summary response?
[03:50] Maya: yes Redwood routing supports fallback policies — can route traffic to cheaper model variant or to a cached fast-response. we can demo the routing rules if you like.
[03:58] Elena: that'll be useful — product cares about graceful degradation.
[04:05] Diego: one more thing — prefix cache hit rate depends heavily on user behavior and seq length. For the internal dataset you shared, hit rate jumped from 14% to 38% after canonicalizing prefix tokens (we stripped timestamps and session IDs). so there's an easy engineering win on the client side to canonicalize.
[04:27] Ravi: good catch. we'll add canonicalization to our client.
[04:30] Jill: on pricing, what's the delta between Hosted and Dedicated for this pilot? we need a predictable monthly commit number for procurement.
[04:40] Maya: base estimate — hosted pay-as-you-go is simpler but more variable; Dedicated reserved capacity (monthly commit) lowers unit cost by roughly 20–35% depending on utilization. I'll send modelled scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[04:55] Jill: procurement will want SLA and SOC2/ISO references. we already asked security and they want KMS integration and audit logs.
[05:05] Diego: we have HSM/KMS integrations and audit logging in the Private/Dedicated stack. note that some of the log delivery requires a customer-managed S3 bucket or syslog forwarder for retention policies.
[05:18] Elena: any regressions in output quality with quantization? you mentioned hallucination uptick. how big?
[05:26] Diego: small but noticeable on our safety prompts — 4-bit quant gave about 2% higher hallucination rate in our automated evals at top-k sampling. deterministic evals less impacted. human evals needed for conversational safety.
[05:40] Ravi: can we run targeted evals only on high-risk prompts? that's faster than full human eval.
[05:46] Diego: yep Diego: we can run focused evals; I can add the high-risk prompt set you gave last month.
[05:54] Maya: timeline wise: Diego will run 16-token micro-batch + 8k prefix + quantization toggle, and include p50/p95/p99 and per-token cost; Customer to share traffic trace; Maya sends pricing.
[06:10] [transcription artifact] Speaker 2: uh yeah mm-hmm
[06:16] Samir: tests on Dedicated look promising but we need to validate VPC egress paths and also the kernel versions on the nodes (some RDMA drivers affect latency). I can add those checks.
[06:30] Diego: noted. i'll include driver/kernel notes in the bench report, plus the exact model binaries used, seed, and temp values.
[06:40] Ravi: curious on cache eviction policies — what's default TTL and how does that affect memory footprint?
[06:47] Diego: default TTL is LRU with a sliding window; we configured 8k prefix retention which gave hit rate improvements and memory footprint stayed within 12GB on the host for that workload. we can tune eviction to favor long conversation sessions.
[07:05] Elena: are there any regulatory concerns with caching user data in the prefix cache? e.g., PII stored in cache?
[07:12] Maya: cache keys are transient and encrypted at rest; for Private deployments you can also configure no-persistence or shorter TTLs plus customer-managed KMS. security appendix covers this.
[07:25] Jill: finance question — if we commit to Dedicated, is there a ramp allowance? we don't want to overcommit early.
[07:33] Maya: yes we typically propose a ramp schedule with buffer months; I'll include a 3-month ramp with utilization targets in the pricing scenarios.
[07:42] Diego: small note on batching: continuous batching can adaptively cut windows if latency SLOs are threatened, so you can get some batching benefits without violating p95 in many cases. but configs matter.
[07:56] Ravi: okay practical next benchmark variants we'd like: 1) 16-token micro-batching + 8k prefix caching; 2) same + fp16 quant (no 4-bit) to check middle ground; 3) Dedicated run for variant 1 to compare variance.
[08:10] Maya: that matches our plan. Diego will run 1 & 2, and we schedule Dedicated run after Samir validates networking.
[08:20] Diego: expected deliverable: bench CSV with columns: config, p50,p95,p99, avg tokens/sec, tokens_per_$, cache_hit_rate, sequence_length_dist. i'll attach the raw logs.
[08:32] Elena: can you also include a simple RUM-style trace example so product can see per-request lifecycle?
[08:40] Diego: yes i'll include sample trace events.
[08:45] [few seconds of crosstalk]
[08:50] Maya: last bit, procurement wants the PO and SOW templates. I'll send those and cc legal.
[08:57] Jill: thanks.
[09:00] Wrap: Confirmed next steps and action items. Plan follow-up the week of 2026-04-13 for dedicated latency deep dive. Thanks all.

End transcript.
